reflexion_entries_to_archive.body: I copied 'CI minutes are a hard constraint' out of e2e.yml's own header comment into my A.0 evidence packet as current fact. One probe refuted it: `gh repo view --json isPrivate,visibility` => PUBLIC, so Actions minutes are free/unlimited on standard runners and the S110 minute-exhaustion story is history. By then it had already reached BOTH Council peers, and Grok built its 'delete the lane' recommendation on it. An in-repo comment is a CLAIM about external state, not evidence of it — Rule 21 exists for exactly this and I applied it to git/CI/service state but not to repo visibility. Fix pattern: enumerate every external-state noun in the PDR's premises (visibility, billing, quotas, branch protection, service availability) and probe each one, including the ones a file appears to answer.

The census limit went 1500 -> 75 -> 30 -> 40 and the last one passed by ONE object. I treated each failure as 'pick a better constant' and re-derived a constant three times. The actual message was in the PATTERN: a value that keeps being overtaken by the next sample is dimensionally wrong. Once I modelled it properly, both the leak signal (t/30) and the noise (~t/220) scaled with the window, so their ratio was window-independent (~7.3x) and the correct assertion was a FRACTION of the signal — which holds ~2.6x over noise and ~2.9x under signal at EVERY window, something no constant could do. It also dissolved two CHECK findings structurally instead of patching them. Trigger to watch for: the second time a threshold needs retuning, stop tuning and check the units.

GROK-ANALYST proposed a tick-SCALED census limit in CHECK. I rejected it as 'empirically refuted', citing that the largest delta (+13) came at the smallest window and that two ~8.2k windows gave D0 and D20. That reasoning was n=4-and-an-outlier. At n=7 the delta clearly scales (max 13 at ~2.2k vs max 39 at ~7.6-8.9k; 3.9x window vs 3.0x noise) and I adopted Grok's shape after rediscovering it the long way. The failure was not trusting-or-distrusting the reviewer — it was quoting a sample as if it were a law, in the same session whose own PDR said 'n=3 cannot support a new threshold value'. When rejecting a reviewer's SHAPE (not their number), the bar is a mechanism or a power-adequate sample, not the three points I happen to hold.

My evidence packet recorded the worker determinism oracle (failed===false, hashMismatches===0) as 'stable across all attempts' in CI. It had NEVER EXECUTED for worker-heap:333: the tick-floor expect() earlier in the shared auditWindow() helper threw first, so every assertion below it was silently unreached — and on a continue-on-error lane that is invisible. I read the numbers that WERE logged and assumed the assertions that follow them had run. This also made the fix more valuable than the PDR claimed: removing the floor is what lets the oracle actually run. Fix pattern: when a test fails, the assertions AFTER the failing line produced no evidence at all — never cite them as passing, and prefer ordering cheap invariant checks BEFORE any environment-dependent gate.

Coupling MIN_VALID_TICKS to CENSUS_LIMIT_OBJECTS introduced a temporal dead zone (ReferenceError at module init) that cost a full 16-minute soak run to discover, because e2e/** sits outside tsconfig.json's include:['src'] so neither `npm run typecheck` nor `npm run build` covers it. Two ~2-second checks would have caught it: `npx playwright test <spec> --list` (forces module evaluation) and `npx tsc --noEmit` pointed explicitly at the spec files. Both are now recorded as standing habits in LOCKED_DECISIONS §15.4. General rule: when a file is outside the project's type-check net, add an explicit cheap gate rather than relying on the expensive end-to-end run.

check_result: 2 findings ADOPTED from the external pair, 3 REJECTED with reasons, and RALPH:PATROL returned SHIP-WITH-FIXES with all 5 fixes applied. REJECTED: Grok M2 (compares against a 4000-tick CI window that never existed — at HEAD the test failed outright and detected nothing; Gemini independently concurred) and L1 (an artifact of a redacted prompt). Grok M1's tick-SCALED census limit was initially REJECTED on n=4 evidence and is now ADOPTED — it was the right shape all along.

what_worked: Pulling the raw CI job log first. The headline finding (all 5 failures are one tick-floor assertion, zero threshold breaches) inverted the handoff's framing and killed option (b) in the first 10 minutes.

Reading src/main.ts for the mechanism instead of curve-fitting the symptom. The dt clamp + PHYSICS_HZ=60 => <=3 ticks/rendered-frame explained the tick shortfall, killed three candidate options at once (including my own), and is now LOCKED so nobody re-derives it.
Spending 6 minutes on ONE local run to obtain the missing datum rather than adopting Gemini's census number on CI-only evidence.
Grep-verifying both peers' central claims before triage: Grok's anti-(e) baseline was phantom, Gemini's anti-(d) oracle claim was already covered by the GATING lane.
what_to_do_differently: Probe every external-state noun in a premise, INCLUDING ones a repo file appears to answer. A code comment is a claim, not evidence.
When a threshold needs retuning a SECOND time, stop tuning and check the units. Three constants died before the dimensional model appeared.
Do not quote a small sample as a law, especially while rejecting a reviewer's shape — the same PDR that said 'n=3 cannot support a threshold' used n=4 to reject Grok M1.
Order cheap invariant assertions BEFORE environment-dependent gates, so a slow runner cannot silently void the assertions that actually matter.
For files outside tsconfig's include, add an explicit cheap gate (--list, targeted tsc) instead of discovering load-time errors 6 minutes into a soak.
